PYTHON · TKINTER · MATPLOTLIB

What happens when
two masses pull on each other?

My Python project calculates gravitational force and simulates the motion of two bodies. Enter two masses and their separation, then watch their paths develop.

The original Python project

Tkinter handles the inputs. Newton's law gives the force, and the program updates velocity and position in small time steps. Matplotlib draws both trails in a 3D plot; the supplied initial conditions keep the motion in a plane.

force = G * m1 * m2 / distance**2
vel1[i] += force / m1 * d[i] / distance * dt
pos1[i] += vel1[i] * dt

About this browser version

This is a JavaScript adaptation made for this portfolio, not the Python program running in your browser. It adds a rotatable Canvas view, adjustable presets, and a velocity-Verlet integrator to limit energy drift.

A few simulation details

The two point masses interact through Newtonian gravity. The simulation uses normalized units internally, then converts force and distance to SI units. Each numerical step is fixed; playback speed changes how many steps run, not their size. No pre-recorded paths or video are used.

It is an educational model, without collisions, physical body surfaces, or relativistic effects. Trails show recent positions.

02 SWIFT · SWIFTUI · SWIFTDATA

Elite Hypertrophy

A gym app for planning workouts, recording sets, and keeping track of progress.

My fitness app brings the workout plan and the live session together. The set logger keeps weight, reps, effort, and rest time in one place.

  • During a workoutLog sets, use a rest timer, and get progression suggestions based on recorded effort.
  • Between workoutsBuild a training split, review exercise progress, and inspect training volume on a muscle map.
  • Importing a workoutUse Vision OCR to extract a workout from a screenshot, then review it before saving.
Under the hood

The iOS app uses SwiftUI for its interface and SwiftData for local workout records. Other parts of the project include a research-assisted coach, progress photos, and StoreKit subscriptions.

The interesting engineering problems include retaining an unfinished session, keeping workout history consistent, and making suggestions understandable while someone is in the middle of a set.
